info.title: qscheduler
info.description: Scheduling service dispatching tasks to quantum computing backends.

get.summary: Health check. Reports whether the service is up and able to reach the database.
Get a machine's configuration. The backend token is not returned.

put.summary:
Replace a machine's configuration (fields omitted from the body get their default values).
The machine is restarted with the new configuration, as on a service restart: queued tasks
and sessions are kept, tasks already handed to the backend are re-attached, and an open
session is closed (its unfinished tasks are cancelled). New tasks and sessions are rejected
with HTTP 409 while the restart is in progress.

delete.summary:
Remove a machine. Without `force`, only a machine without any tasks and sessions is
removed. With `force`, its tasks and sessions are deleted as well, and jobs already handed
to the backend get a best-effort cancel request.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description:
Remove the machine even if it has tasks or sessions; they are deleted together with
their consumption records (the consumed time is not returned to their projects).

409.description: The machine has tasks or sessions and `force` is not set

get.summary: Describe the machine's backend: its type and version information.
Fetch a calibration data set from the backend.

post.summary:
Suspend a machine. While suspended, the machine rejects every new task and session
(including tasks submitted into an already open session) with HTTP 409 and the suspension
message. Existing work is handled according to `cancel`.

422.description: `message` is empty or longer than 512 characters

delete.summary:
End a machine's suspension; it accepts new tasks and sessions again. Work failed or closed
by the suspension stays so.

get.summary:
List a machine's suspensions, newest first. The active suspension, if any, is the first
entry and has no `resumed_at`.
List all machines, sorted by name. Backend tokens are not returned.

post.summary: Register a machine. It accepts tasks and sessions right away.

409.description: A machine with this name already exists

get.summary: List registered notifiers, sorted by name. Tokens are not returned.

post.summary:
Register a notifier — an HTTP callback target for task and session events. It can be
selected by new tasks and sessions right away.

409.description: A notifier with this name already exists

422.description: Invalid name (empty or longer than 512 characters) or URL

delete.summary:
Remove a notifier. Events already queued for it are still delivered; tasks and sessions
that use it stop sending notifications.

post.summary:
Register a project — a named, time-accounted budget that tasks and sessions are charged
against.

409.description: A project with this name already exists

get.summary: Get a single project by name.

patch.summary:
Update a project's `active` flag and/or time `limit_ms`. Fields omitted from the request
body are left unchanged. Does not affect `consumed_ms`.

post.summary:
Create a session — a time-bounded, exclusive reservation of one machine for one project.
Tasks in the session are cancelled when the session closes.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Name of the project the session's time is charged to.

parameters.name: notify
parameters.description:
Name of the notifier to send the session's open/close events to. No notification is
sent when omitted.

402.description: The project has exceeded its time limit, or the project is not active.

409.description: The machine is suspended (the body contains the suspension message), or is being reconfigured or removed.

422.description: Unknown `project` or `notify`, or `time_limit_ms` exceeds the machine's `--max-session-time`.

get.summary: Get a session's current info (state, timings, and its machine/project).

delete.summary:
Request cancellation of a session. Cancellation is asynchronous: a queued (`"waiting"`)
session is removed from the queue, while an `"open"` session is closed and its tasks are
cancelled (both those already submitted to the backend and those still queued); in both
cases the session eventually reaches the `"closed"` state.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description:
Session to associate the task with. The session must be in the `"open"` state or the
task is rejected. Exactly one of `project` / `session_id` must be given.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
Name of the project to charge the task's time to. Exactly one of `project` / `session_id`
must be given.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Free-form identifier of the user submitting the task, stored alongside the task.

parameters.name: time_limit_ms
parameters.description:
Maximum execution time in milliseconds, counted from when the backend starts running
the task. When exceeded, the task is cancelled and ends `failed`. Defaults to the
machine's default task time limit.

parameters.name: notify
parameters.description:
Name of the notifier to send the task's completion event to. No notification is sent
when omitted.

requestBody.description: Raw task payload forwarded to the backend.

402.description: The project has exceeded its time limit, or the project is not active.

409.description: The machine is suspended (the body contains the suspension message), or is being reconfigured or removed.

422.description: Neither or both of `project`/`session_id` given, unknown `machine`/`project`/`notify`, `time_limit_ms` is zero, or the session is invalid or not open.

get.summary: Get a task's current info (state, timings, and its session/project/machine/user).

delete.summary:
Request cancellation of a task. Cancellation is asynchronous: a queued task is removed from
the queue, while a running task is cancelled on the backend; in both cases the task
eventually reaches the `"cancelled"` state (poll `GET /tasks/{id}` to observe it).

409.description: Task already in a terminal state (finished, failed, or cancelled)

get.summary:
Fetch a named artifact produced for a task from the backend that ran it, forwarded
verbatim (no caching, no parsing).

200.description: Raw artifact JSON as returned by the backend

409.description: Task has not been submitted to a backend yet

get.summary:
Fetch a task's raw result from the backend that ran it, forwarded verbatim (no caching,
no parsing).

200.description: Raw result JSON as returned by the backend

409.description: Task has not been submitted to a backend yet

machine_name.description: Machine name on the IQM server.

poll_interval_ms.description: Job status polling interval, in milliseconds.

BackendRequest.description: The backend a machine dispatches its tasks to.

BackendResponse.description: A machine's backend as reported by the API (without its token).

oneOf.description: Versions reported by the IQM server's `/about` endpoint.

name.description:
Unique notifier name (at most 512 characters); tasks and sessions select the notifier
by it in their `notify` field.

token.description: Token included in every event payload.

url.description: URL to POST task completion and session open/close events to.

active.description: Whether the project can accept new tasks/sessions.

IqmVersion.description: Version fields of the IQM `GET /about` response; other keys are ignored.

oneOf.description: The active suspension, if the machine is suspended.

MachineSettings.description: A machine's configuration. Omitted fields get their default values.

default_task_time_limit_ms.description: Time limit of tasks submitted without an explicit `time_limit_ms`, in milliseconds.

limit_check_interval_ms.description:
How often session consumption is stored into the DB and task time limits are checked,
in milliseconds.

max_clock_skew_ms.description: Maximum assumed lag of the backend's clock behind ours, in milliseconds.

max_session_time_ms.description: Maximum duration a session on this machine may request, in milliseconds.

queue_size.description: Maximum number of tasks submitted to the backend at once.

NotifierInfo.description: A registered notifier as listed by the API (without its token).

has_token.description: Whether event payloads include a token.

active.description: Whether the project can accept new tasks/sessions.

consumed_ms.description: Time consumed so far, in milliseconds.

SessionInfo.description:
A snapshot of a session's public-facing data, resolved names and all — the shape returned
by `GET /sessions/{id}` and embedded in the session open/close callback.

closed_at.description: Absent unless the session has closed.

exectime_ms.description: Milliseconds of execution time consumed by tasks run during this session, if any.

notify.description:
Name of the notifier that receives the session's open/close events. Absent if the
session was created without `notify`, or its notifier has since been removed.

opened_at.description: Absent if the session never opened (still waiting, or closed while still queued).

project.description: Name of the project the session's time is charged to.

SessionStateKind.description: The current state of a session, as a plain string (no embedded data).

SuspendCancel.description: What happens to a machine's existing work when it is suspended.

message.description:
Why the machine is suspended (at most 512 characters). Returned in the error of every
rejected task/session submission, and in the error of every task failed by `cancel`.

Suspension.description: A machine suspension — the active one, or a past one from the history.

resumed_at.description: Absent while the suspension is still active.

TaskInfo.description:
A snapshot of a task's public-facing data, resolved names and all — the shape returned by
`GET /tasks/{id}` and embedded in the task completion callback.

exectime_ms.description: Milliseconds of execution time consumed, if any.

finished_at.description: Absent if the task is still `waiting` or `running`.

notify.description:
Name of the notifier that receives the task's completion event. Absent if the task was
submitted without `notify`, or its notifier has since been removed.

project.description:
Name of the project the task's time is charged to, if it was project-parented directly
(not via a session). Mutually exclusive with `session`.

session.description: Session the task ran in, if it was session-parented. Mutually exclusive with `project`.

started_at.description: When the backend started running the task. Absent until then.

time_limit_ms.description:
Execution time limit in milliseconds, counted from `started_at`. When exceeded, the task
is cancelled on the backend and ends `failed`.

TaskStateKind.description: The current state of a task, as a plain string (no embedded data).

active.description: Whether the project can accept new tasks/sessions. Omit to leave unchanged.

limit_ms.description: Time budget, in milliseconds. Omit to leave unchanged.
